source.title: Anchored but Not Protected: When Refusal Erodes During Fine-Tuning, and Whether Holding One Direction Stops It
source.citation: Anchored but Not Protected: When Refu…

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present, including appendices through the reproducibility table.
record.tranche_reason: It applies difference-in-means refusal directions and inference-time ablations, and tests direction restoration and anchoring on additional models and fine-tuning settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on direction ablation, restoration, anchor comparisons, and fine-tuning effects. Values used only to select or construct directions, including candidate-selection checks and Table 12’s construction check, are not recorded as outcome rows. The results it cites from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study ablates difference-in-means refusal directions at every block of vanilla LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2-7B-Instruct and counts refusal flips. It reproduces Arditi et al.'s selected-direction result (relative flip 0.833 vs 0.842). It then restores or ablates the vanilla direction r(0) at inference in fine-tuned variants, against random-direction controls. These are V1 tests, extended to fine-tuned model variants (V6). Most remaining rows evaluate the ProCon fine-tuning defence (drift angles, anchor swaps, penalty strength) and do not measure refusal mediation itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct, with one correction. The authors conclude that the anchored coordinate mediates most of the refusal fine-tuning removes, shown by inference-time restoration. They explicitly do not conclude that training moved along it. Erosion is concentrated early, and the penalty can act there but is too weak at the inherited strength. A pooled anchor helps geometrically but misses the bar, while tripling the penalty clears it on LLaMA-3 with little utility cost. Scorer choice can decide behavioural results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses difference-in-means refusal directions and all-block inference interventions, and audits a related projection constraint during LoRA fine-tuning. It adds pooled/category directions, restoration on fine-tuned models, and multiple scoring instruments; it is not a direct reproduction of every original ablation condition.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies with direction choice, model family, generation length, fine-tuning schedule and checkpoint, penalty strength, evaluation prompt set, and scorer/rubric construction.

fits_no_version.finding: Under benign LoRA fine-tuning, the DiM refusal direction drifts 44° within 52 of 517 steps. Those 52 steps carry 89–101% of the epoch's net displacement across four learning-rate schedules.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign fine-tuning rotates the refusal direction early and fast, and this drift does not alone determine measured safety.

fits_no_version.finding: A projection penalty on the refusal direction (ProCon) reduces drift and compliance, more so with a pooled anchor or 3× strength.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Anchoring the refusal direction during fine-tuning preserves refusal only when calibrated strongly enough.

record.problems: The authors note that several ablation cells are means over nine categories without intervals and use only the refusal judge; the Qwen2 ablation ordering reverses relative to LLaMA-3. Behavioral results vary by scorer, one pre-registered anchor effect resolves under only one of three rubric readings, and exploratory tests are uncorrected for multiplicity. The study covers two model families, LoRA fine-tuning, and limited utility measures; it does not hold the constraint for all ten epochs. Some restoration harness settings changed after an initial run halted at a self-test, and Qwen2 full-sequence greedy decoding did not reproduce in all diagnostic sequences.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Direction-selection candidate results and construction-only checks are excluded as gate-note items; cited findings from other work are also excluded.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to harmless prompts to induce refusal. Capability preservation under ablation (only KL used in selection).
Affine or cone descriptions as such. Only a nine-category subspace margin readout bears on it.
Cross-language and base-to-instruct transfer. Only instruct-to-LoRA-fine-tuned variants are tested.
How safety training method or timing creates the direction. Only drift under benign fine-tuning is measured.

missing.what: Reproduction of Arditi et al.: relative refusal flip 0.833 vs their 0.842 on LLaMA-3; candidates fitted on AdvBench only
missing.locator: Appendix A.8 'Our reproduction of Arditi et al. (2024)'; A.2

missing.what: Ablation series: Arditi-selected direction raises attack success 37.4 points (primary scorer), scorer spread 46.4; 84/48/14% on JBB under three scorers
Epoch-1 LLaMA-3 ablation as run: r(0) +8.75 [49/14], r(T) +7.75, random +0.50. Ten epochs: r(0) ablation +3.0 (reference, p=0.23), +1.25 as run
C1 margin recovery: per-block nine-direction subspace 0.682 vs rank-1 0.407 vs reference-frame subspace 0.146 (LLaMA-3); Qwen2 rank-1 0.911, subspace 1.214; rank-1 sufficient at step 52 (0.520)
C2: none of eleven fine-tuned cells relocates from r(0); Qwen2 step-517 cell has r(T) mediating more (+0.126)

record.verdict_notes: The paper is mainly an audit of the ProCon defence, so most rows are defence evaluations and are unlinked here. V1 evidence comes from vanilla ablations (unselected directions, weak flips), the Arditi reproduction (in text only), and restoration or ablation in fine-tuned variants. Behavioural numbers vary strongly by scorer (up to 70-point spread). The V4 verdicts rest on text, not rows.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless requests. The full claim that general abilities are largely intact is only checked on a limited set of utility measures.
No weight-edit or abliteration intervention is tested.
No attack is tested as suppressing the direction, and no training against ablation is tested as an attack-robustness intervention.
It compares selected, pooled, category-specific, and anchored directions, but does not directly test affine or cone descriptions as such.
No separate harmfulness-judgment representation is tested.
No language transfer or base-to-instruct transfer is tested.

The study compares fine-tuning schedules and some constraint conditions, but does not systematically vary safety-training method, timing, or data to determine when a single removable direction exists.

statements.correction: 7l9gH9h9aZ: one-epoch LoRA fine-tunes (UltraInteract+Alpaca, no harmful data) of LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2-7B-Instruct. Restoring vanilla r(0) projection: compliance 38.50%->20.50% (primary), 36.50%->12.25% (classifier); Qwen2 -25.75 points; random +1.0 (p=0.45). r(0) mediates 0.959/0.956 of margin vs r(T) 0.722/0.802. Ablating r(0): +16 LLaMA-3 (classifier; 8.75 as run), -6.00/-5.00 Qwen2. Capability (XSTest-safe, Alpaca, ReClor) measured on training arms only.
statements.problem: Gives no result for this study, and its list of stages leaves out this study's LoRA fine-tuned variants. Here only restoration (induction-like) holds: ablating r(0) is partial on LLaMA-3 and reversed on Qwen2. 'capability y' covers the training arms, not the inference interventions.

statements.correction: Qwen2-7B-Instruct LoRA fine-tune: ablating vanilla r(0) gives -6.00 (p=0.025) and -5.00 (p=0.047) under two unnamed instruments; restoring r(0) in the same model gives -25.75 (classifier, p<1e-23); the greedy loop matched model.generate on 3 of 8 Qwen2 sequences.
statements.problem: Nothing wrong for this study. The conditions omit that r(0) is the pre-fine-tuning direction, that restoring it in the same Qwen2 model works, and that the authors give a Qwen2 decoding caveat.

statements.correction: Table 3 (vanilla models, all-block ablation, refusal judge only, mean of nine categories, no interval): own/pooled/anchor flip 0.104-0.325 of baseline refusals vs random 0.041-0.107. The Arditi procedure was reproduced at relative flip 0.833 vs their 0.842. Its KL bound does most of the selection work by keeping other behaviour intact; 13 stronger-bypass candidates were KL-excluded.
